record.category: anonymous pomf clone (1 GiB per file)

free_tier.stated: Max upload size is 1 GiB, wow!
free_tier.notes: No account, no email, no cap on the number of files stated.

per_object_cap.notes: 1 GiB is the largest anonymous per-file cap met among debrid providers that is both stated and on a host that answers.

retention.stated: unverified: the homepage publishes no expiry and the FAQ was not readable as text (served gzip without a decoded body to the reader)
retention.notes: The Terms & Privacy page is the place to settle it; it was not read.

egress.terms: Downloads are served from pomf2.lain.la; no byte allowance and no download counter are published.

record.interface_detail: POST https://pomf.lain.la/upload.php multipart field 'files[]'. JSON reply with success, files[0].url, .hash (SHA-1), .size. The stored object is served from the pomf2 host.
record.tooling: curl -F 'files[]=@file' https://pomf.lain.la/upload.php; an optional 'speedkey' field exists for a queue priority the site calls Speedkeys
record.chaining: 1 GiB per object with no account is the right shape for a single large media file or a dataset shard: two files cover a 2 GiB upload that most relays refuse, and the JSON reply carries SHA-1 so the store can be verified without a second download.
record.limits_note: The homepage HTML carries a comment saying a PHP CVE took uploads down and that they are back, which is the vendor's own note that the stack is patched reactively.
record.binding_note: At 1 TiB a month this is 1 024 objects of 1 GiB; the cap is what forces splitting, and no rate or byte counter was observed to bind first.

identity_cost.detail: Multipart POST with no account, no email and no cookie; a link came back.

record.reliability_note: Uploads were switched off during a PHP CVE and switched back on, per a comment left in the homepage HTML; treat availability as hobby-grade.
record.confidence_note: Upload, read-back and SHA-256 match in on 2026-10-23, at 1 MiB. The 1 GiB claim is the vendor's and was not pushed to.

evidence.proved: read-back 1 048 576 bytes, sha256 da0099c231f1182a5d411c8ac5149dfb7a2e3578a3970928490cb78ba92aecc9, full-body hash matched
'Max upload size is 1 GiB, wow!' and the comment that uploads had been disabled for a PHP CVE and are back

record.notes: The caveat is retention, which nobody states: a 1 GiB cap is worth nothing if the file is gone in a week, and that is the one number still missing.
